passage.title: The Rise of a Chinese Social Media Sensation
passage.text:
In China, it has become increasingly common for ordinary people to become famous almost overnight through short videos and live broadcasts on the internet, especially among younger users. These new online celebrities are often called 'wanghong,' a term that simply means someone who is very popular online. Unlike traditional celebrities such as actors or singers, many wanghong become famous without any special training or professional background, sometimes purely by chance rather than deliberate planning or years of hard work and careful study beforehand.

Often, the rise to fame begins with a single short video that unexpectedly attracts millions of views within just a few days. The video might show something funny, surprising, or simply relatable, and viewers quickly share it with their friends and family members across different platforms and apps. Within days, the person in the video can go from being completely unknown to having millions of followers watching everything they post online. This sudden change can feel exciting and thrilling, but it can also be confusing and overwhelming for the person experiencing it firsthand.

Once someone becomes popular online, many choose to start livestreaming, where they talk directly to their followers in real time for hours at once, often late into the night. A large number of these livestreams focus on selling products, from clothing to cosmetics to food, directly to viewers who are watching from home. This type of online shopping has grown extremely quickly in China, and some of the most successful livestreamers can sell millions of dollars worth of products in a single evening alone, far more than most traditional stores could ever manage to sell.

Becoming famous so quickly can bring both real benefits and serious difficulties for the people involved. Many new celebrities earn large amounts of money in a remarkably short period of time, more than they ever expected when they first started out in life. At the same time, they often face constant attention from the public, with every action they take being closely watched and sometimes harshly criticized online. Some people struggle to handle this sudden pressure, especially when negative comments appear unexpectedly and spread quickly across social media platforms.

Perhaps the most difficult lesson for many wanghong is that online fame rarely lasts forever, no matter how popular someone becomes at first. Internet trends change extremely quickly, and audiences can lose interest in someone just as fast as they once became genuinely interested in them. Because of this, many successful online celebrities try to create new content constantly, hoping to stay relevant before their followers move on to someone new and more exciting. This constant pressure to remain popular is something few people expect when they first become famous online, and it rarely disappears completely.

passage.title: The Influence of Son Tung M-TP on V-Pop
passage.text:
Vietnamese popular music, commonly referred to as V-pop, has undergone considerable transformation over the past decade, and few individual artists are credited with shaping that transformation as consistently as Son Tung M-TP. His emergence in the early 2010s coincided with a broader shift in Vietnamese youth culture toward globally influenced aesthetics, a convergence that arguably amplified his impact well beyond what his music alone might have achieved on its own considerable merits.

Son Tung's early releases drew criticism from some quarters for their apparent resemblance to South Korean and American pop production styles, an accusation that trailed him for several years even as his popularity grew rapidly among younger audiences across the country and well beyond its borders. Rather than abandoning this cross-cultural approach, he gradually incorporated elements more explicitly rooted in Vietnamese musical and visual traditions, a shift that critics have since interpreted as a deliberate attempt to carve out a distinctly Vietnamese identity within an unmistakably global pop framework.

This blending of influences became particularly evident in music videos that paired contemporary production values with imagery drawn from Vietnamese folklore, historical costume, and traditional instrumentation, presented alongside choreography and visual effects comparable to major international productions of similar scale and ambition. Whether this represents genuine cultural synthesis or a more calculated commercial strategy remains a matter some critics continue to debate, though the resulting content undeniably reached audiences considerably beyond Vietnam's borders.

Beyond his music itself, Son Tung's business ventures, including his own entertainment company, have positioned him as an influential figure within the Vietnamese entertainment industry more broadly, one whose commercial decisions shape opportunities for younger artists attempting to enter the same competitive space. This dual role, as both a performer and executive with structural influence over other careers, distinguishes his position from that of many contemporaries whose impact remains confined largely to their own musical output alone, without such broader reach.

His influence also extends into how Vietnamese artists approach international audiences, since several of his releases achieved measurable engagement on global platforms in ways that were considerably less common for Vietnamese pop music prior to his emergence onto the scene. Younger artists have since adopted similar strategies, releasing music with English-language elements or internationally oriented visual styles, an approach that industry observers frequently trace back, at least partially, to the commercial precedent he established years earlier in his career.

Critics of his influence, however, caution against overstating the extent to which V-pop's broader international visibility can be attributed to any single artist, noting that streaming platforms, social media distribution, and Vietnam's growing economic profile likely would have expanded the genre's international reach regardless of any particular performer's individual career trajectory or personal creative choices made along the way.

Whether Son Tung M-TP's specific contribution to V-pop's evolution represents a uniquely decisive influence or simply the most visible example of broader structural changes already underway remains, among industry analysts, a genuinely open question that resists easy resolution one way or the other, even after considerable and sustained debate on the matter over recent years.

passage.title: The Secrets of Deep-Sea Exploration
passage.text:
More is known, by most accounts, about the surface of the Moon than about the deepest regions of Earth's own oceans, a comparison that sounds implausible until one considers just how inhospitable and technically demanding deep-sea environments remain even with today's most advanced modern technology and equipment. Less than a quarter of the ocean floor has been mapped in any real detail, leaving vast stretches of the planet's largest habitat almost entirely unexamined by scientists.

The obstacles confronting deep-sea exploration are formidable, beginning with pressure that increases roughly one atmosphere for every ten meters of depth, reaching levels in the deepest ocean trenches that would crush most conventional equipment almost instantly. Complete darkness below a few hundred meters eliminates any possibility of natural light, and near-freezing temperatures combined with corrosive saltwater place additional strain on instruments designed to survive such punishing conditions for extended periods of time.

Early exploration relied heavily on manned submersibles, vessels capable of carrying human crew to extreme depths, though the considerable expense and risk involved limited how frequently such ambitious missions could be undertaken safely. Remotely operated vehicles, controlled from surface ships via long cable, gradually assumed much of this exploratory burden, offering researchers extended dive times and reduced risk to human life, albeit at some cost to the intuitive, hands-on observation that manned missions had historically provided to scientists in the field.

Among the most significant discoveries to emerge from this ongoing exploration were hydrothermal vents, first documented in the late 1970s, where mineral-rich water heated by volcanic activity beneath the seafloor supports entire ecosystems that exist entirely independent of sunlight. Organisms clustered around these vents derive energy through chemosynthesis rather than photosynthesis, a discovery that fundamentally challenged prior scientific assumptions about the specific conditions necessary for complex life to exist at all.

This finding carries implications extending well beyond marine biology alone, since it suggests that life might plausibly emerge and persist in environments previously considered far too extreme to support it, a consideration directly relevant to astrobiologists searching for life on distant moons such as Europa and Enceladus, where subsurface oceans may harbor conditions broadly analogous to Earth's own hydrothermal systems below the seafloor.

Growing interest in deep-sea mineral deposits, particularly polymetallic nodules containing metals essential to modern battery production, has introduced a competing set of priorities into deep-sea exploration that scientific researchers did not originally anticipate having to navigate carefully. Mining companies argue that these resources could reduce reliance on environmentally destructive land-based extraction methods, while marine biologists caution that disturbing deep-sea ecosystems, many of which remain barely documented, risks eliminating species and processes before they can even be properly studied and understood by researchers.

Whether scientific exploration and commercial extraction can proceed in genuine balance, or whether one will inevitably come to dominate deep-sea policy at the other's expense, remains an unresolved tension that international regulatory bodies have only just begun to address seriously in recent years. What seems reasonably certain is that decisions made over the coming decade will shape deep-sea ecosystems in ways that may prove difficult, if not entirely impossible, to reverse later on.

    • Với R3Q1, quét từ khóa "deep-sea exploration", "difficult" ở đoạn 2: áp suất cực lớn và bóng tối gần như hoàn toàn (extreme pressure and near-total darkness) khiến việc khám phá vô cùng khó khăn.

    • Với R3Q8, quét từ khóa "mining companies", "deep-sea deposits" ở đoạn 6: các công ty khai thác lập luận rằng việc khai thác dưới đáy biển có thể làm giảm sự phụ thuộc vào việc khai thác trên đất liền (reduce reliance on land-based extraction).
  • Dạng câu hỏi Loại trừ NOT (R3Q4): Đối soát các ưu điểm của phương tiện điều khiển từ xa (ROV) ở đoạn 3: giảm rủi ro cho con người (reduced risk to human life), kéo dài thời gian lặn (extended dive times), điều khiển qua dây cáp từ tàu mẹ. Chi tiết "loại bỏ hoàn toàn việc quan sát trực tiếp của các nhà khoa học" là thông tin sai lệch/loại trừ.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Từ vựng theo ngữ cảnh (R3Q2, R3Q9): Sử dụng kỹ năng Context Clues (Manh mối ngữ cảnh):
    • Với R3Q2, từ "formidable" ở đoạn 2 mô tả các trở ngại gian nan của biển sâu, do đó đồng nghĩa với cực kỳ khó khăn (extremely difficult).
    • Với R3Q9, từ "analogous" ở đoạn 5 mô tả sự tương đồng giữa điều kiện ở biển sâu Trái Đất với môi trường trên các mặt trăng băng giá, do đó đồng nghĩa với có thể so sánh/tương đồng (comparable).
  • Dạng câu hỏi Quy chiếu (R3Q6): Tập trung vào đại từ "it" ở đầu đoạn 5: "This finding carries implications... since it suggests that...". Từ "it" thay thế trực tiếp cho phát hiện khoa học được đề cập ngay trước đó ("This finding").
  • Dạng câu hỏi Suy luận (R3Q7): Phân tích logic từ đoạn 5 về việc sự sống tồn tại nhờ hóa tổng hợp không cần ánh sáng Mặt Trời. Có thể suy luận rằng sự sống có thể tồn tại ở những môi trường khắc nghiệt hơn nhiều so với quan niệm trước đây.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Mục đích của tác giả (R3Q10): Phân tích bố cục tổng thể toàn bài. Tác giả trình bày xuyên suốt từ khó khăn công nghệ, phát hiện khoa học đến các mâu thuẫn lợi ích nhằm giải thích về các phát hiện cùng những căng thẳng chưa được giải quyết trong khám phá biển sâu.

Lời khuyên: Ưu tiên giải quyết trước các câu hỏi định vị rõ ràng như Từ vựng (R3Q2, R3Q9) và Quy chiếu (R3Q6). Tiếp theo, áp dụng kỹ thuật đọc quét nhanh để hoàn thành các câu hỏi Chi tiết (R3Q1, R3Q5, R3Q8) và câu hỏi Loại trừ (R3Q4). Cuối cùng, tổng hợp logic toàn bài để chọn đáp án chuẩn xác cho nhóm câu hỏi tư duy gồm Ý chính (R3Q3), Suy luận (R3Q7) và Mục đích của tác giả (R3Q10).

passage.title: The Psychology of Urban Noise and Well-being
passage.text:
Not only has urban noise long been dismissed as a mere nuisance rather than a genuine public health concern, but the psychological mechanisms through which chronic noise exposure actually damages well-being remain considerably less understood than the physiological hearing damage that dominates most public discussion of the topic. Whether policymakers have adequately grasped this distinction, given how noise regulation continues to focus overwhelmingly on decibel thresholds rather than psychological impact, remains genuinely doubtful among researchers who study the issue closely and continuously.

Chronic exposure to urban noise appears to activate stress response systems even when the noise itself falls below levels capable of causing measurable hearing damage, a finding that complicates regulatory frameworks built primarily around auditory harm thresholds alone. Elevated cortisol levels, disrupted sleep architecture, and cardiovascular strain have all been documented in populations exposed to persistent traffic or aircraft noise, effects that manifest gradually over years rather than appearing as an immediate, easily attributable response to any single noise event.

Sleep disruption in particular has attracted growing research attention, since noise need not fully wake a sleeper to disrupt the deeper sleep stages associated with physical and cognitive restoration. [1] Even noise events too brief or quiet to produce conscious awakening can measurably shift sleep architecture toward lighter stages, reducing the restorative benefit of a full night's rest without the sleeper ever realizing their sleep quality has been compromised. [2] This subtlety helps explain why many urban residents report feeling chronically fatigued despite believing they obtained adequate total sleep duration each night. [3] Researchers studying this phenomenon face a persistent methodological challenge: self-reported sleep quality frequently diverges considerably from what objective physiological measurements actually reveal about the body. [4]

Cognitive performance represents another domain where noise exposure produces effects considerably more subtle than outright hearing damage, particularly among children whose developing auditory processing systems appear especially vulnerable to chronic background noise exposure. Studies comparing students in noisier versus quieter school environments have found measurable differences in reading comprehension and memory tasks, differences that persist even after controlling for socioeconomic factors that often correlate with noise exposure in ways that could otherwise confound such comparisons entirely.

Psychological adaptation to noise, while real, appears considerably more limited than commonly assumed, since physiological stress responses frequently persist even after residents report having grown accustomed to their acoustic environment subjectively over time. This disconnect between subjective habituation and continued physiological strain suggests that self-reported tolerance may provide a misleading basis for regulatory decisions, since residents who no longer consciously notice noise may nonetheless continue experiencing its measurable health effects regardless.

Socioeconomic disparities compound these effects considerably, since lower-income urban residents disproportionately live near major roads, airports, and industrial zones, meaning that noise-related health burdens overlap substantially with other forms of environmental and economic disadvantage already well documented in public health research more broadly. Addressing noise exposure in isolation from these broader structural inequities, some researchers argue, risks treating a symptom of urban inequality as though it were an independent, freestanding environmental problem in itself.

Whether future urban planning and noise policy will adequately incorporate psychological research alongside more traditional auditory safety standards remains, at this stage, a genuinely open question that will likely depend on how effectively researchers can translate complex physiological findings into policy frameworks that regulators and urban planners can practically implement and enforce over time.

tasks.suggestion:
Để đạt kết quả tốt cho phần thi này, bạn nên áp dụng các chiến thuật sau đây:

  • Dạng câu hỏi Ý chính (R4Q1): Sử dụng kỹ năng Skimming (Đọc lướt). Đọc các câu chủ đề: đoạn 1 mở đầu bằng nhận định ô nhiễm tiếng ồn đô thị bị coi thường/đánh giá thấp (dismissed as a mere nuisance) và ảnh hưởng tâm lý của nó chưa được chú ý đúng mức; các đoạn tiếp theo chứng minh tác động đến giấc ngủ, nhận thức và sức khỏe thể chất. Lựa chọn đúng phải phản ánh trọn vẹn việc tác giả trình bày tiếng ồn đô thị như một vấn đề sức khỏe thực sự bị đánh giá thấp (underappreciated health concern).
  • Dạng câu hỏi Chi tiết (R4Q2, R4Q9): Sử dụng kỹ năng Scanning (Đọc quét từ khóa) để tìm dữ kiện trực tiếp có sẵn trong bài đọc:
    • Với R4Q2, quét các từ khóa "affect sleep without waking": âm thanh vẫn có thể làm dịch chuyển cấu trúc giấc ngủ (sleep architecture) sang các giai đoạn nông hơn mà người ngủ không hề tỉnh giấc (without waking up).
    • Với R4Q9, quét từ khóa "socioeconomic factors": chính sách xử lý tiếng ồn cần phải tính đến cả các yếu tố kinh tế - xã hội do sự phân bổ tiếng ồn liên quan đến bất bình đẳng đô thị.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Loại trừ NOT (R4Q4): Đối soát các tác động được nhắc tới trong bài: gia tăng nồng độ cortisol, xáo trộn cấu trúc giấc ngủ, ảnh hưởng khả năng đọc hiểu của học sinh. Chi tiết "Mọi trẻ em tiếp xúc với tiếng ồn đều bị suy giảm thính lực vĩnh viễn" là thông tin tuyệt đối hóa và sai lệch so với bài đọc.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Chèn câu (R4Q5): Phân tích tính logic ngữ cảnh tại vị trí [2] ở đoạn 3. Câu trước [2] mô tả việc tiếng ồn làm dịch chuyển cấu trúc giấc ngủ sang các giai đoạn nhẹ hơn mà người ngủ không hề nhận ra. Câu chèn bổ sung: "Tác động này xuất hiện rõ rệt hơn ở người lớn tuổi, những người vốn đã có cấu trúc giấc ngủ tự nhiên nông hơn" giúp phát triển trực tiếp ý về sự dịch chuyển cấu trúc giấc ngủ trước khi vế [2] kết luận về lý do tại sao nhiều cư dân bị mệt mỏi mạn tính.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Từ vựng theo ngữ cảnh (R4Q3, R4Q8): Sử dụng kỹ năng Context Clues (Manh mối ngữ cảnh):
    • Với R4Q3, từ "confound" ở đoạn 4 mô tả sự phức tạp làm rối/khó phân biệt các yếu tố tác động đến nhận thức, do đó đồng nghĩa với khó phân biệt/làm nhiễu (difficult to distinguish).
    • Với R4Q8, từ "habituation" ở đoạn 5 đi kèm ngữ cảnh cư dân cảm thấy quen thuộc/quen dần với tiếng ồn theo thời gian, do đó đồng nghĩa với việc quen dần với cái gì đó (growing used to something).
  • Dạng câu hỏi Quy chiếu (R4Q6): Tập trung vào đại từ "it" ở đoạn 6: "Noise exposure is not evenly distributed... which means it interacts with...". Từ "it" quy chiếu trực tiếp đến sự tiếp xúc với tiếng ồn (noise exposure).
  • Dạng câu hỏi Suy luận (R4Q7): Phân tích logic ở đoạn 5 về hiện tượng cư dân thích nghi tâm lý (habituation). Việc cư dân nói rằng họ đã quen với tiếng ồn không có nghĩa là cơ thể họ đã ngừng phản ứng căng thẳng về mặt sinh lý (Feeling accustomed to noise may not mean the body has stopped reacting).
  • Dạng câu hỏi Mục đích của tác giả (R4Q10): Phân tích bố cục tổng thể toàn bài. Tác giả phân tích các tác động tâm lý và sinh lý ngầm của tiếng ồn nhằm giải thích lý do tại sao các ảnh hưởng tâm lý của tiếng ồn đô thị đáng nhận được nhiều sự chú ý hơn từ các nhà chính sách.

Lời khuyên: Ưu tiên giải quyết trước các câu hỏi định vị rõ ràng như Từ vựng (R4Q3, R4Q8), Quy chiếu (R4Q6) và Chèn câu (R4Q5). Tiếp theo, áp dụng kỹ thuật đọc quét nhanh để hoàn thành các câu hỏi Chi tiết (R4Q2, R4Q9) và câu hỏi Loại trừ (R4Q4). Cuối cùng, kết nối bức tranh logic toàn bài để chọn đáp án chuẩn xác cho nhóm câu hỏi tư duy gồm Ý chính (R4Q1), Suy luận (R4Q7) và Mục đích của tác giả (R4Q10).
